stem: In the figure, point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(AD = BD\). The measure of angle \(BAC\) is \(84^{\circ}\), and the measure of angle \(ABC\) is \(38^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ADC\)?
solution: Because \(AD = BD\), triangle \(ABD\) is isosceles and angle \(BAD\) = angle \(ABD = 38^{\circ}\).
Angle \(ADC\) is an exterior angle of triangle \(ABD\), so it equals the sum of the two interior angles not next to it: \(38 + 38 = 76^{\circ}\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]==P['D'][1] and P['B'][0]<P['D'][0]<P['C'][0]
assert abs(d('A','D')-d('B','D'))<0.01 and abs(ang('B','A','C')-84)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','B','C')-38)<0.1
ans=38+38
assert abs(ang('A','D','C')-ans)<0.1
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==76
